enable_confidence_scores.description: When true, includes a per-label confidence score in the response.

enable_rationales.description: When true, includes a rationale explaining each classification in the response.

instructions.description: Natural-language guidance that steers how the text is classified (up to 20,000 characters).

multilabel.description: When true, allows more than one label to be returned per input.

version.description: The function version to invoke. Defaults to the latest version. Supported versions: ["2.1"].

content.description: The content to classify. It accepts a plain string or the response object of [ai_parse_document](:method:AiFunctions/AiParseDocument).

labels.description: The label set to classify as. Either a JSON array of label strings (e.g. ["spam", "not_spam"]), or a JSON object mapping each label to a description (e.g. {"spam": "unsolicited bulk message", "not_spam": "a legitimate message"}). Accepts 2 to 500 labels, each 1 to 100 characters.

options.description: Function options. Omitted fields fall back to their documented defaults.

metadata.description: Additional metadata returned by AI Classify.

response.description: The function result as a JSON value. An array of per-label objects: one element in single-label mode (the default), or multiple elements when `multilabel` is true. When `enable_confidence_scores` and `enable_rationales` are true, `confidence_score` and `rationale` are included in each response value, respectively.

version.description: The function API version to invoke. Defaults to "1.0". Supported versions: ["1.0"].

options.description: Function options. Omitted fields fall back to their documented defaults.

state.description: A string, JSON object, or array containing the content, related context, and examples needed to answer the provided questions. For example, provide a support message, a conversation, or records describing the current state of an application. All questions receive this same state.

metadata.description: Metadata identifying the function API version used for this request.

version.description: The function API version used to evaluate the request.

aifunctions.AiExtractBbox.description: A bounding box on a source page; used by bbox-input citations.

coord.description: Pixel coordinates on the page image as [x0, y0, x1, y1].

page_id.description: 0-based page index the box is on.

aifunctions.AiExtractCitation.description: A citation locating an extracted value in the source. start/stop are set for span (STRING input) citations, bbox for bbox (parsed-document input) citations.

bbox.description: Bounding boxes locating the citation on the source pages; set for bbox citations.

id.description: Integer matching a citation_ids entry on an extracted field.

start.description: Inclusive 0-based character offset into the input string; set for span citations.

stop.description: Exclusive 0-based character offset into the input string; set for span citations.

enable_citations.description:
When true, includes citation metadata locating each extracted value in the source. Depending on the type of input, citations can be one of two types:

For raw text (STRING) inputs, a citation is a span of text in the original input. Each object in `metadata.citations` has an `id` (integer matching a `citation_ids` entry on a field), a `start` (inclusive 0-based character offset into the input string), and a `stop` (exclusive 0-based character offset into the input string).

For PDF documents and images (when using ai_extract downstream of ai_parse_document), a citation is a bounding box in the original input. Each object in `metadata.citations` has an `id` (integer matching a `citation_ids` entry on a field) and a `bbox` (array of {coord, page_id} objects, identical in shape to element.bbox in ai_parse_document output; coord is pixel coordinates on the page image as [x0, y0, x1, y1], and page_id is a 0-based page index).

enable_confidence_scores.description: When true, includes a per-field confidence score in the response.

instructions.description: Natural-language guidance that steers how data is extracted (up to 20,000 characters).

mode.description: Extraction mode. Supported modes: "precision" — more powerful extraction for complex schemas, long documents, and reasoning-heavy extractions. Defaults to none (standard extraction).

version.description: The function version to invoke. Defaults to the latest version. Supported versions: ["2.1"].

content.description: The text to extract from. It accepts a plain string or the response object of [ai_parse_document](:method:AiFunctions/AiParseDocument).

options.description: Function options. Omitted fields fall back to their documented defaults.

schema.description: The extraction schema defining the fields to extract. Either a JSON array of field names, assumed to be strings (e.g. ["company", "valuation"]), or a JSON object mapping each field to its type/description/nullability (e.g. {"company": {"type": "string", "description": "the company name"}}). Accepts up to 256 fields, 12 levels of nesting, and 500 enum values. Supported field types are string, integer, number, boolean, and enum.

metadata.description: Additional metadata returned by AI Extract.

response.description: The function result as a JSON value. When `enable_confidence_scores` and `enable_citations` are true, `confidence` and `citation_ids` are included in each response field, respectively.

chunk_type.description: How the source was chunked for citation offsets (span for text input, bbox for parsed-document input); present when citations are enabled.

citations.description: Citation objects locating each result in the source; present when citations are enabled.

mode.description: The resolved extraction mode; present when a non-default mode was used.

aifunctions.AiParseDocumentFileMetadata.description: Metadata about the source file; present only for file-path input.

file_modification_time.description: Last-modified timestamp of the source file, as an HTTP date string.

file_name.description: Base name of the source file.

file_path.description: Unity Catalog volume path of the source file.

file_size.description: Size of the source file in bytes.

description_element_types.description: Element types for which an AI-generated description is produced. Use "*" (default) to generate descriptions for all supported element types, "figure" to generate them for figures only, or "" (empty string) to generate none. Only figure descriptions are supported for version "2.0", so "*" and "figure" produce the same behavior.

image_output_path.description: Unity Catalog volume path where rendered page and element images are written.

page_range.description: Pages to parse (1-indexed), as a comma-separated list of page numbers or ranges (e.g. "1,3,5-10").

version.description: The ai_parse_document output schema version. Supported value: "2.0".

aifunctions.AiParseDocumentPageError.description: A single page that failed to parse while the overall request succeeded.

error_message.description: Message describing why the page failed.

page_id.description: 0-based index of the page that failed.

content.description: The document to parse. The REST API accepts a Unity Catalog volume path to the source file or a base64 data URL containing the file bytes (for example, data:application/pdf;base64,<encoded-file-bytes> or data:image/jpeg;base64,<encoded-file-bytes>). Supported formats: PDF, DOCX, DOC, PPTX, PPT, JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF. Accepts up to 100 pages and 100 MB per document.

options.description: Function options. Omitted fields fall back to their documented defaults.

document.description: The parsed document as a JSON value, containing the extracted pages and elements.

error_status.description: Per-page partial-failure details; present when the request succeeds (2xx) but individual pages fail.

metadata.description: Additional metadata returned by AI Parse Document.

file_metadata.description: Describes the source file; present only for file-path input.

id.description: Unique identifier for the parse request.
